briefing.opening: Good day. We begin the Climate Daily Briefing for November 23, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Empty-Handed Conclusion After 17 Years… COP31 Talks Collapse, Exposing a Total Impasse in Climate Diplomacy
sections.content: The 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31), held in Antalya, Türkiye, failed to adopt a final declaration after participating nations could not bridge differences over the phase-out of and transition away from fossil fuels [5, 6, 12]. Marking the longest-running climate summit in history, the conference concluded without any official agreement for the first time in 17 years, laying bare the limitations of the multilateral climate negotiation framework [24, 160, 161]. In response, Pacific island nations and African countries facing the brunt of climate disasters expressed deep despair, while climate leaders including Al Gore strongly urged reform of the UN conference's 30-year-old consensus-based decision-making rule [22, 132, 155, 165].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 First Major Overhaul of Korea's Renewable Energy Market in 15 Years… RPS Abolished and Shift to Contract Market
sections.content: The South Korean government has decided to phase out the existing Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) and fully transition to a competitive bidding-based contract market starting in 2027 [76, 78, 83]. Accordingly, fixed-price contracts and competitive bidding systems will be introduced for new solar and wind installations starting next year, fundamentally restructuring the power generation pricing mechanism [71, 75, 80]. To minimize market confusion stemming from the regulatory shift and to gather broad public and industry input, the government plans to host an information session on November 27 to unveil the details of the reform plan [77, 81].

sections.title: ⚠️ Climate Change Threats Striking Health, Agriculture, and Ecosystems: Research and Responses Underway
sections.content: As the climate crisis poses increasing threats to human survival and broader ecosystems, the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency has launched a comprehensive analysis of health-vulnerable populations categorized by age and underlying conditions, while gathering multidisciplinary input on climate impacts on public health [1, 7, 18]. In the agricultural sector, the Rural Development Administration is establishing high-temperature damage criteria, refining meteorological data, and promoting the distribution of 'Baromi 4,' a new climate-resilient crop variety; meanwhile, major production hubs in the United States face crises in cranberry harvests—a traditional holiday crop—due to warmer winters [10, 21, 163]. Furthermore, ecological warning signs continue across the globe, including the rapid disappearance of Antarctic sea ice and the destruction of the habitat of Madagascar's rare golden mantella frog [2, 167].

sections.title: 🌱 Combining AI and Clean Energy… Accelerating the Green Transition and Public-Private Partnerships
sections.content: In Seoul, the 'Korea Carbon Forum 2026' was convened to explore solutions for overcoming the climate crisis in the AI era, focusing on green transition growth strategies integrated with advanced industries [15, 19, 43, 46]. In the private sector, H Energy, GS Energy, and STIC Investments signed a joint development agreement for a 1 GW nationwide rooftop solar power initiative, moving to expand distributed clean energy [82, 89, 103]. Additionally, South Korea and Qatar held their first policy consultation in five years, agreeing to expand bilateral cooperation in solar energy, efficiency-focused renewables, and the AI sector [73, 84, 96].

briefing.closing: Even amid the deadlock in global climate negotiations, the importance of practical industrial transition and on-the-ground action continues to grow. That concludes today's climate briefing.
